b: A great idea is a judgment. The current world should be better.
I Have a Great Idea Really Means …
#1. I have a job for you.
Listen closely. That excited voice has extra work for you.
They want you to do something that will make their life better.
Enthusiasm comes easy when someone else does the work.
Ask: What role will you play in making this happen?
#2. I see a problem you need to fix.
Seeing a problem is easier than fixing it. Any fool can see something others should fix.
Ask: What have you done to solve this?
#3. I want you to change your priorities.
An idea is a baby and we love our babies. You should love their baby too.
The message: Drop what you’re doing so you can nurture my baby.
Ask: What are you willing to own?
“We could” often means “You could.” Volunteering others is a control freak’s paradise.
“We need to” often means “You need to.”
“Wouldn’t it be great if…” often means “Wouldn’t it be great if you…”
“We ought to” often means “You ought to.”
Don’t let other people’s brilliant suggestions run your life.
Practice openness. Some new ideas are great. Say things like:
What do you see that makes this a great idea?
What will it take to make this work?
What needs to change if we do this?
What are you willing to do to make this happen?
Don’t become the dumping ground for other people’s brilliance.
Great ideas are easy when someone else does the work.
How can leaders nurture ideas without letting others run their lives?
